title: Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs
one_line: Institutions sell to raise month-end cash (peak at T-4 under 3-day settlement, pushing prices down T-8 to T-4) and buy back from T-1 to T+3; US stocks earned about +25 bps in the T-3 to T-1 reversal and ~+48 bps T-3 to T+3 (1995-2013).

findings.statement: Monthly cycle around the last trading day T: T-8..T-4 'selling pressure' (avg daily -0.03%, abnormal ≈ -37 bps/month); T-3..T-1 'positive reversal' (avg daily +0.12%, ≈ +25 bps); T..T+3 buying pressure (T-3..T+3 ≈ +48 bps); T+4..T+8 negative reversal.
2003-2013: cumulative excess returns in the T-3..T-1 window were 103%, about 73% of the market's total excess return.
Timing follows settlement: 3-day settlement pushes month-end selling to T-4; Europe's move to 2-day settlement (Oct 2014) shifted the pattern (T-2 autocorrelation fell by 0.78, t ≈ -3.2 to -3.7).
Reversals are 2-3x larger when the month ends on a Friday (pension + weekly salary cycles coincide).
Present in 20 of 23 developed markets; strongest in large, liquid stocks.

why.pattern: Institutional constraint / payment cycles: funds must raise cash for month-end payouts and do it at predictable, settlement-determined times.
why.mechanism: Pension and fund payouts at month end → selling timed by settlement lag (T-4 under T+3) → price pressure, then reversal and re-investment buying T-1..T+3.
why.who_is_forced: Mutual funds, pensions and other institutions meeting month-end cash obligations.
why.why_it_persists: Payment calendars and settlement rules are fixed; agency concerns delay selling to the last moment.
why.what_would_kill_it: Settlement changes (US moved to T+2 in Sept 2017 and T+1 in May 2024 — the window should shift accordingly), spreading of payouts across the month.
why.authors_explanation_vs_ours: Agree; key for us is that the window must be shifted with each US settlement change.

reported_results.headline: T-3..T-1 ≈ +25 bps/month, T-3..T+3 ≈ +48 bps; T-8..T-4 ≈ -37 bps.
key_stats: 2003-2013: T-3..T-1 window = 73% of market excess return

tradable_edge: Long ES from the close of the peak-selling day to month end (+3 days); flat (or short) during the selling window. Settlement-adjusted timing: T+3 era (to Sept 2017) buy at close T-4; T+2 era (Sept 2017-May 2024) buy at close T-3; T+1 era buy at close T-2. Exit at close T+3.
angles: Settlement-adjusted long window vs the naive TOTM window (baseline)

decay_risk.reason: Published 2020; structural cash cycle, but settlement changes shift the timing.

data_fit: ES 1-min (ETH + RTH) Dec 2013 → Sep 2026 in clean_ES_master.parquet; NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026. 2024+ is protected in the backtest project. Daily closes from 1-min bars; ~120 months in 2014-2023.
caveats: Several results 'available on request'; mutual fund flow data only 2007-2013.
Sample ends before the US T+2 (2017) and T+1 (2024) changes.
